gates.name: IG-01 Confirm thread arc type (story / teardown / listicle-lesson
gates.description: Confirm thread arc type (story / teardown / listicle-lesson / data drop) before drafting tweet 1.

gates.name: IG-02 Confirm thread length target (5-12 tweets); threads >12 requ
gates.description: Confirm thread length target (5-12 tweets); threads >12 require a written justification.

gates.name: IG-03 Refuse 'thread' formatting for content that fits one tweet —
gates.description: Refuse 'thread' formatting for content that fits one tweet — bloat is a halt.

gates.name: IG-04 Confirm whether a link is included; links suppress reach, so
gates.description: Confirm whether a link is included; links suppress reach, so their placement is decided up front.

gates.name: CG-01 Arc contract
gates.description: Thread arc and payoff stated in one sentence; tweet count declared.
gates.command: $SESS/arc.yaml parses with keys arc_type, payoff, tweet_count; validator exits 0

gates.name: CG-02 Tweet 1 contract
gates.description: First tweet <=280 chars, states the payoff or the tension, contains no 'A thread:' filler, and no link.

gates.name: CG-03 Per-tweet atomicity
gates.description: Every tweet stands alone (one idea), <=280 chars, numbered consistently, no dangling 'this' references.
gates.command: `python3 scripts/thread_atom.py $SESS/thread.md` exits 0 (checks each block: length, atomicity, anaphora lint)

gates.name: CG-04 Payoff delivery
gates.description: Declared payoff from arc.yaml appears by the penultimate tweet; final tweet is recap + follow/reply CTA <=200 chars.

gates.name: CG-05 Evidence tweet
gates.description: >=1 tweet contains a concrete number, named source, or artifact reference for data/teardown arcs.
gates.command: `grep -cE '[0-9]+%|source:|study|v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' $SESS/thread.md` >= 1 for data arcs; recorded waiver otherwise

gates.name: CG-06 Link placement rule
gates.description: Zero links in tweets 1..N-1; any link lives in final tweet or a declared reply.

gates.name: CG-07 Media spec
gates.description: Any attached image is 1600x900 or 1080x1080, <5MB, alt text written.
gates.command: For each asset: `python3 scripts/img_size.py --allow 1600x900,1080x1080 --max-mb 5 $SESS/assets/*` exits 0; alt text lines in $SESS/alt.txt match asset count

gates.name: CG-08 Voice & repetition lint
gates.description: No banned tokens; no sentence opener repeated >2x across the thread.

gates.name: CG-09 Proof packet seal
gates.description: Thread text, arc, and asset hashes sealed; tweet 1 logged to anti-repeat ledger.
gates.command: `sha256sum -c $SESS/proof/packet.sha256` exits 0; ledger append verified by line-count delta == 1

preconditions.startup_phrase: I am the Thread operator. Tweet 1 is a contract; every tweet after pays it off in <=280 characters each; the last tweet earns the follow.

self_improvement.pattern_cadence: After every 5 sessions, mine the JSONL log for recurring gate failures, degrade waivers, and proof-command runtime outliers; write findings to ~/.rig/logs/harnesses/patterns/twitter-thread-session-patterns.md.
self_improvement.update_trigger: If any single gate fails in >=30% of logged sessions over a rolling 20-session window, OR a new platform constraint (algorithm change, policy update, format deprecation) invalidates a proof command, propose a harness revision: bump the gate's proof, adjust its threshold, or split the gate — then re-seal with a new version hash.

success_conditions: Tweet 1 passes the contract check with no filler and no link.
Every tweet atomic and within length; payoff delivered before the final tweet.
Link placement and media specs machine-verified.
Proof packet sealed; tweet-1 hook in the repetition ledger.
failure_states: halt: Stop the session immediately. Record the failing gate id, the proof command output, and the missing prerequisite in $SESS/proof/halt_log.yaml. Do not draft past a halt gate; resume only after the gate's proof exits 0.

degrade: Continue the session with the deficit logged in $SESS/proof/waivers.md (gate id, reason, owner). A degrade-tier failure blocks 'clean ship' status — the Definition of Done must record the waiver explicitly.

stop: Terminal condition. Seal whatever proof exists, write $SESS/proof/stop_reason.md, and exit. No outward action (publish, send, deploy) may follow a stop-tier failure without human Gate-D approval.

final_rule: Ship only what the gates can prove. No artifact leaves this session on adjectives — every claim is bound to a command, a file, or a hash. A blocked gate is information, not failure; log it, learn from it, and make the next session's proof stronger. The operator who follows this harness leaves the system stronger than it found it.
